Staff Backend Engineer, Freight Visibility Platform
Meridian Freight Systems — Remote (US)

About the role
Meridian builds the real-time visibility layer that enterprise shippers use to track freight across road, rail, and ocean. We ingest telemetry from several thousand carrier integrations and turn it into ETAs our customers plan operations around. When our numbers are wrong, someone's dock crew stands idle.

We're hiring a Staff Backend Engineer to own the ingest and event distribution path end to end. This is a deep systems role on a small team, not a coordination role.

What you'll do
Own the telemetry ingest pipeline: partitioning, deduplication, backpressure, and the storage model underneath it
Design the event contracts that a dozen downstream consumer teams depend on, and the compatibility rules that keep them from breaking each other
Drive the multi-region work as we take on customers with data residency requirements
Set the technical direction for the platform group and bring senior engineers along with you — mentorship is an explicit part of this role, not an extracurricular
Participate in a light on-call rotation for the services you own, backed by real runbooks and blameless postmortems

Requirements
7+ years building and operating backend services in production
Deep experience with Go, or comparable depth in another statically typed language plus a willingness to work in Go daily
Strong PostgreSQL fundamentals — schema design, query performance, and knowing when the relational model is the wrong tool
Production experience with Kafka or an equivalent event streaming platform, including schema evolution and consumer group operations
Demonstrated experience designing distributed systems that hold up under sustained load growth
Comfort operating on AWS and in Kubernetes

Nice to have
Domain experience in logistics, supply chain, freight, or transportation
Terraform or comparable infrastructure-as-code experience
gRPC and protobuf for internal service communication
Time-series storage at scale (TimescaleDB, ClickHouse, or similar)
Observability practice — OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, and the judgment to know which signals are worth alerting on

How we work
Remote-first since founding, with quarterly on-sites
Written-first culture: proposals and ADRs before implementation on anything expensive to reverse
Blameless postmortems, and error budgets that actually pause feature work when they burn
Individual contributor track goes to Principal with no requirement to manage people
